newsitem.title: USA: Republicans see lower U.S. deficit.
newsitem.headline: Republicans see lower U.S. deficit.

text.p: Congressional Republican budget committee leaders said on Sunday the U.S. budget deficit for the financial year that ended Sept. 30 will be about $109 billion, the lowest in a decade.

They released the figure, which is still not official, an hour after White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta hinted on a television interview programme that President Bill Clinton will have "some good news" on the U.S. budget deficit.
"We'll have some good news on the deficit front," Panetta said on CNN's "Late Edition" programme.
Taking credit before Clinton could, the chairmen of the House and Senate budget committees promptly issued a pre-emptive press release.

They said that they estimate the deficit for fiscal year 1996 is about $55 billion lower than for fiscal year 1995 and about $7 billion lower than the $116 billion figure projected by the Congressional Budget Office in August.
They said it was no thanks to Clinton whose re-election on Nov. 5, along with a majority of Democrats in Congress, would lead to "a blank check for higher deficits in the years to come."

House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich of Ohio said that "this accomplishment comes as good news to every American but a complete surprise to Bill Clinton who should get absolutely no credit for it."
Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici of New Mexico said the lower deficit "vindicates our willingness to stand up to Bill Clinton."
